site.name: Noor Guide
site.subtitle: First lessons in Islam
site.description: Learn the foundations of Islam at your own pace: belief, prayer, the Quran and daily supplications, with the source of each teaching named.

home.title: Learn the foundations of Islam, one lesson at a time.
home.subline: Free, with no account, in English, Arabic and French.
home.shahadaTitle: I have just taken my shahada
home.shahadaBody: Follow the path in order, from what Muslims believe to wudu and your first prayer.
home.exploringBody: Start with what Muslims believe, and why, without signing up for anything.
home.pathIntro: Nine parts, each building on the one before.
home.sourcesQuran: The Arabic of the Quran is quoted from published editions of the text, with its surah and verse. Its meaning is given in the Saheeh International translation.
home.sourcesHadith: Each hadith gives its collection and number so you can look it up. Translations of hadith, du'as and the words said in prayer are our own unless marked otherwise.
home.sourcesReview: Most of the rulings have not yet been checked by a scholar, so ask a local imam or teacher before relying on a detail. Where the schools of Islamic law differ, the lessons say so.

learn.dashboardIntro: Take the parts in order: each builds on the one before. Your progress stays in this browser.
learn.continueTitle: Pick up where you left off
learn.glossaryLead: Met a word you do not know?
learn.glossaryLink: The glossary explains the common terms and phrases.

lesson.schoolsNote: The schools of Islamic law differ on some details of this lesson. A local imam or teacher can explain them.
lesson.memorizationHelper: Read the Arabic first, then show the transliteration to check yourself.

salah.rakahSubheading: Each unit of prayer follows these steps. The number of rakaat varies by prayer; see the table above.

surahs.translationNote: The English meanings on this page are the Saheeh International translation.

glossary.subtitle: Essential Islamic terms and everyday Arabic phrases.

tools.title: Everyday tools
tools.subtitle: For praying on time, facing the qibla and finding a mosque near you.
tools.prayerTimesBody: Today's five prayer times for where you are.
tools.qiblaBody: The direction of the Kaaba in Makkah from where you are.
tools.masjidFinderBody: Open a map of the mosques near you.

location.manualHelp: For example 51.05, -114.07. Two decimals are enough.
location.manualInvalid: Enter a latitude from -90 to 90 and a longitude from -180 to 180, separated by a comma.
location.privacy: Your location stays in this browser; rounded coordinates go to <host>api.aladhan.com</host> for prayer times and to the map you open when you search for a mosque, and the qibla is worked out on this device.
location.errorPermissionDenied: Location permission was denied. Enable location access in your browser settings, or enter coordinates manually.
location.errorUnavailable: Unable to determine your location. Try again or enter coordinates manually.
location.errorTimeout: Location request timed out. Try again or enter coordinates manually.
location.errorUnsupported: Geolocation is not supported in your browser. Please enter coordinates manually.

prayerTimes.title: Prayer times
prayerTimes.subtitle: View the five daily prayer times for your location.
prayerTimes.errorNetwork: The prayer-time service could not be reached.
prayerTimes.errorService: The prayer-time service did not answer as expected.
prayerTimes.errorRetry: Check your connection and reload the page.
prayerTimes.staleNote: The prayer-time service could not be reached, so these are the times saved for {date}.
prayerTimes.footerNote: Prayer times are calculated from your location and the selected method. Times may vary slightly from your local mosque. Where possible, follow your local mosque's schedule.

qibla.title: Qibla direction
qibla.subtitle: The direction of the Kaaba in Makkah from your location.
qibla.trueNorthNote: Measured from true north. A phone compass shows magnetic north, which can differ by several degrees depending on where you are.
qibla.aboutBody: The qibla is the direction Muslims face in prayer: toward the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) in Makkah.

masjidFinder.title: Find a mosque near you
masjidFinder.subtitle: Locate mosques in your area for congregational prayers and community.
masjidFinder.osmSearchBody: A free map made by the people who use it.
masjidFinder.tipsHeading: Tips for finding your local mosque
masjidFinder.tip1: Search for "mosque", "masjid", or "Islamic center" in your area.
masjidFinder.tip2: Many mosques welcome new Muslims and have programmes for reverts.
masjidFinder.tip3: Don't be shy to visit during prayer times. The community will be happy to help.
masjidFinder.tip4: Friday (Jumu'ah) prayer is a great first visit. Arrive early to meet people.

progress.title: Your progress
progress.subtitle: What you have finished so far. It is kept in this browser only.
progress.resetConfirmBody: This clears every lesson you have marked as done, and it cannot be undone.

notFound.title: This page is not here
notFound.body: The link may be old or mistyped. Go back to the start, or carry on with the lessons.
